q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a retail store per square foot?
title: Retail store carbon per square foot
short: Divide the store's electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, plus generator diesel and refrigerant top-ups, by the carpet area in square feet. Report each store per month, and keep refrigerated stores apart, since chillers and freezers use far more energy per square foot.
audience: Retail chains and franchise store owners

ul: Refrigerant top-ups for AC and display chillers.

p: In a mall, your own metered electricity is Scope 2. Common-area charges are Scope 3, Category 8, unless you control that space.
Use carpet area from the lease, and compare stores of the same format, since grocery and apparel stores differ widely.

example.title: Worked example: one apparel store (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Total: 6,658 / 3,000 = 2.219 kg CO2 per sq ft a month
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use each store's bill and lease area.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
